facts.text: DClawPoseFixed-v0 is registered with the entry point robel.dclaw.pose:DClawPoseFixed and max_episode_steps 80
The DCLAW3_ASSET_PATH constant of a pose task is robel-scenes/dclaw/dclaw3xh.xml
The pose episode counts 80 steps of 20 simulation steps at 2.5 ms each (4 s)
An environment step skips 20 simulation steps by default
The DClaw group covers nine joints with position ranges -0.48 to 0.48 rad, -PI/3 to PI/3 rad and -PI/2 to PI/2 rad repeated three times, and a velocity range -2*PI/3 to 2*PI/3 rad/s
The normalized action space is a Box from -1.0 to 1.0 with one element per joint position
An action is clipped to -1.0 to 1.0 before it is applied
The denormalization center is the mean of the actuator range and its range is half the span of that range
A normalized action is clipped to -1.0 to 1.0 and denormalized with the actuator center and range
A joint-position command is clipped to the qpos range and then its velocity is clipped to the qvel range
The default observation keys are qpos, last_action and qpos_error
get_obs_dict returns qpos, qvel, last_action and qpos_error, where qpos_error is the desired pose minus the current qpos
The flat observation is the concatenation of the selected observation arrays
The observation space is a Box from -inf to +inf with the observation shape
A reset sets last_action to None
When no action has been taken, the last-action observation is a zero array
DClawPoseFixed resets to a random initial pose and a random desired pose
A random pose clamps the upper bound of the middle joints at indices 1, 4 and 7 to 0
The pose reward is the negative norm of qpos_error minus 0.1 times the norm of the qvel entries whose absolute value is at least pi
The default get_done returns an all-false array, so the pose environment does not terminate by itself

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds the environment and draws both poses from the seeded generator, so one seed and one action sequence repeat a trajectory; upstream draws with numpy's generator and this package's fake with Python's random.Random, so a seed gives different poses and a different trajectory on the two

gaps: the fake backend is a kinematic stand-in for MuJoCo: it moves each joint toward the normalized position target through the clipped desired velocity, resolves no contacts, actuator forces, gear friction, damping or sensor model, and the MuJoCo engine was never run here
the fake draws the initial and desired poses with Python's random.Random, while upstream uses numpy's generator, so one seed gives different poses and trajectories on the two
the fake does not apply the registered 80-step TimeLimit that gym.make wraps around DClawPoseFixed-v0: an episode in the fake ends only on reset
the fake does not model rendering or the safety scores, and it serves the fixed-pose task only (not the random or random-dynamics variants)
snapshot and restore are not offered: the fake exposes no get_state/set_state, and upstream's get_state covers only qpos/qvel, not the desired pose or the random generator
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no physical DClaw is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
